more.def: To have a certain price.
examples: The book costs ten dollars.
How much does a pizza cost?
That bike costs more than my allowance.

easy.def: Clothes you wear to look like someone or something else.
examples: I wore a costume at Halloween.
The costume is a tiger.
Her costume was a witch.

more.def: Special clothes that you wear to look like another person, animal or character.
examples: She wore a tiger costume for Halloween.
The actors changed into their costumes before the play.
He made a robot costume from a cardboard box.

easy.def: A long, soft seat for two or more people.
examples: We sit on the couch.
The cat sleeps on the couch.
The couch is soft.

more.def: A long, soft seat with a back and arms, where several people can sit.
examples: We watched a movie on the couch.
The cat curled up on the couch for a nap.
Dad put a blanket on the couch.

easy.def: To push air out of your throat with a loud sound.
examples: I cough when I have a cold.
He coughed.
Please cover your mouth when you cough.

more.def: To push air out of your throat suddenly and loudly.
examples: She coughed because of the dust.
Cover your mouth when you cough.
I coughed all night with my cold.

easy.def: A loud noise from your throat when you are sick.
examples: I have a cough.
The cough is bad.
She has a dry cough.

more.def: The sudden, loud sound made when you push air out of your throat.
examples: I have a cough from my cold.
His cough kept him awake at night.
Warm tea helped her cough.

easy.def: A group of people who make decisions together.
examples: The town council met.
The council made a rule.
The student council planned a dance.

more.def: A group of people chosen to talk about things and make decisions for a town or school.
examples: The town council voted to build a new park.
The student council planned the school dance.
The council met every Tuesday.

easy.def: To say numbers to find how many.
examples: Count the apples in the bowl.
I counted ten ducks.
She counts her steps.

more.def: To say numbers in order to find out how many there are.
examples: We counted the stars until we fell asleep.
The cashier counted the coins twice.
Count by fives to reach fifty.

easy.def: To matter.
examples: Every vote counts.
Your help counts.
Little things count.

more.def: To be important.
examples: Every vote counts in a class election.
It is not the size of the gift that counts but the thought.
Small steps count when you are training for a race.

easy.def: A land with its own name and leaders.
examples: France is a country in Europe.
Which country do you live in?
Each country has its own flag.

more.def: A land with its own government and borders.
examples: Brazil is the largest country in South America.
Many countries took part in the games.
She visited three different countries on her trip.

easy.def: Land with farms and fields, away from cities.
examples: We drove to the country.
Cows live in the country.
The country is quiet.

more.def: Land outside towns and cities, with farms, fields and woods.
examples: Grandpa's farm is deep in the country, far from any city.
We love hearing the crickets in the country at night.
A country road wound between the hills.

easy.def: A part of a state.
examples: Our county has a fair.
I live in this county.
The county road.

more.def: A section of a state or country that has its own local government.
examples: Our county holds a fair each summer.
The county road runs past the farm.
There are fifty counties in the state.

easy.def: Two things or two people.
examples: I have a couple of toys.
A couple came in.
Wait a couple of minutes.

more.def: Two things or people that are together, or a small number of them.
examples: A couple of ducks swam across the pond.
The married couple waved from their car.
I will be back in a couple of minutes.

easy.def: Being brave.
examples: It takes courage to try new things.
The knight had a lot of courage.
It took courage to pet the big dog.

more.def: The strength to do something even though it is scary or hard.
examples: It took courage to tell the truth about what happened.
The firefighters showed great courage during the rescue.
He found the courage to try out for the school play.

easy.def: A path where people race.
examples: The course is long.
The runners ran the course.
We walked the course.

more.def: A path or area made for racing or playing a sport.
examples: The runners lined up at the start of the course.
The golf course has hills, ponds, and sandy spots.
The rowing course on the river is very long.

easy.def: A set of lessons.
examples: I take a swim course.
She likes the art course.
It is a short course.

more.def: A set of lessons about one subject.
examples: My sister is taking a course in how to paint.
The library offers a free course on how to use computers.
The cooking course lasts for six weeks.

easy.def: A flat place where people play some games.
examples: We play tennis on a court.
The basketball court is full.
He ran across the court.

more.def: A flat, marked area where games such as tennis or basketball are played.
examples: The players ran onto the basketball court.
A tennis court has a net in the middle.
We shoot hoops on the court after school.

easy.def: A place where a judge decides who is right.
examples: The lawyer spoke in court.
The case went to court.
People tell the truth in court.

more.def: A place where a judge decides arguments and questions about laws.
examples: The lawyer spoke to the judge in court.
The case went to court last spring.
The court decided that the rule was fair.

easy.def: The child of your aunt or uncle.
examples: My cousin is my age.
I play with my cousin.
Our cousins visit in summer.

more.def: A relative who is the son or daughter of your aunt or uncle.
examples: My cousin and I built a fort.
Four cousins stayed with us over the summer.
She taught her cousin to ride a bike.

easy.def: To put something over something else.
examples: Cover the soup with a lid.
Snow covers the hill.
She covered the baby with a blanket.

more.def: To put one thing over another to hide it, protect it or keep it warm.
examples: Cover the bowl with plastic wrap to keep the food fresh.
Clouds covered the sun all afternoon.
He covered his ears when the siren went off.

easy.def: A thing that goes over another.
examples: The book has a red cover.
Put the cover on the pot.
The bed has a warm cover.

more.def: A lid, blanket or other thing that goes over something.
examples: The cover of the book shows a dragon.
Put the cover back on the pool at night.
I pulled the cover up to my chin.

easy.def: A big farm animal that gives milk.
examples: The cow says moo.
Cows eat grass.
The cow gives milk.

more.def: A large farm animal that gives milk and is raised for meat.
examples: The cow grazed in the green pasture.
Farmers milk the cows every morning.
A cow can eat grass all day.

easy.def: A person who is too afraid to do what is right or hard.
examples: He felt like a coward for hiding.
The coward ran away.
Do not call anyone a coward.

more.def: A person who is easily scared and does not face danger or something hard.
examples: In the story, the coward hid when danger came.
He felt like a coward for staying quiet.
Being afraid does not make you a coward.

easy.def: A man who takes care of cattle on a ranch.
examples: The cowboy rode a horse.
He wore a cowboy hat.
The cowboy rounded up the cows.

more.def: A worker on a ranch who rides horses and takes care of cattle.
examples: The cowboy rode out at dawn to check the herd.
He wore a big hat and boots like a cowboy.
The cowboys moved the cattle across the plains.
